- S3  cfg(unix) item with a same-name `#[cfg(not(unix))]` sibling in the same scope (module, inherent impl, or crate root). Rows 2, 4, 6, 14, 18. This is #720 generalized beyond crate-root main.rs."

criteria.yes: The item works on PORT-010's result for the #[cfg(unix)] item of such a same-name pair, in any wording and in any direction, alone or with other shapes.

relevant.instructions: Does `item.text` decide, change, keep or defer whether PORT-010 reports a #[cfg(unix)] item that has a #[cfg(not(unix))] sibling of the same name and kind in the same scope, where the scope is a module, an inherent impl, or a crate root (lib.rs, main.rs or a src/bin file) (#720, #786 shape S3), or build what that decision directly needs? Items that mention such same-name pairs only as context for another shape (for example as the callers of renamed functions or of helpers) without changing whether PORT-010 reports the #[cfg(unix)] item of the pair, and items that only require earlier S3 tests or an inventory burn-down to keep passing, are no. Judge subject presence only, whatever the item plans; do not judge whether the item obeys `anchor.statement`.

criteria.no: `item.text` does not commit: it names the issue or shape but leaves the approach to be decided, does groundwork only, covers other shapes only, keeps the finding or hides it with allows, or carves out a scope (such as src/bin files or inherent impls) or an item kind (such as consts or types).
criteria.unclear: `item.text` states an outcome close to this that cannot be read as the full commitment or not.
criteria.yes: `item.text` states, in any wording, that PORT-010 does not report such an item in modules, inherent impls and crate roots, with no scope or item kind carved out.

addressed.instructions: `anchor.statement` requires that PORT-010 not report a #[cfg(unix)] item that has a #[cfg(not(unix))] sibling of the same name and kind in the same module, inherent impl or crate root. Does `item.text` commit to that outcome as part of this item? Saying 'crate root' covers lib.rs, main.rs and src/bin files. Still reporting pairs that differ in name, kind or scope is consistent with the commitment. Judge commitment only, not conflict. Work on other shapes, such as un-gated or differently named alternatives, helpers of paired callers or rejected-config accessors, commits nothing to this outcome, even when it also stops a PORT-010 report.

criteria.no: `item.text` does not: it removes the finding in all those scopes, is silent, defers, or keeps findings only outside that situation.
criteria.unclear: `item.text` describes PORT-010's treatment of such items in wording that cannot be read either way.
criteria.yes: `item.text` says or sets a rule under which such an item keeps its PORT-010 finding in some listed scope or for some item kind.

contradicted.instructions: Does `item.text` plan that PORT-010 keeps a finding, shown or hidden, on a #[cfg(unix)] item whose #[cfg(not(unix))] sibling has the same name and kind and sits in the same module, inherent impl or crate root (lib.rs, main.rs or a src/bin file)? Examples: PORT-010 reports or keeps reporting such an item in any of those scopes; the exemption covers only some scopes (for example lib.rs and main.rs but not src/bin files, or not inherent impls); only #[cfg(windows)] twins count; only some item kinds count while same-name, same-kind consts, statics or types stay reported; or the finding is kept and hidden with a per-site allow, exclusion or allowlist. Not this: planning that such items stop being reported; silence; deferral or groundwork; work on other shapes; still reporting an item whose #[cfg(not(unix))] counterpart is in a different scope, has a different name, or is a different kind of item. Judge conflict only.

relevant.instructions: `anchor.statement` governs whether sc-lint's PORT-010 rule reports the declaration line of a `#[cfg(unix)] mod x;` module (shape S6 in atm-core issue #786). First identify which PORT-010 shapes or cases `item.text` says its rule change covers. The subject is touched when that coverage includes the cfg(unix) module declaration or S6, when the item names that declaration or S6 to keep, suppress, refactor, or defer it, or when the item undertakes to fix every #786 PORT-010 false positive. The subject is not touched when the rule change is limited to other named shapes or cases, even if the item also re-extracts every #786 file as a fixture, labels findings by shape, or lists other shapes as not closed; nor by work on other rules or configuration. Judge subject overlap only, not whether the item obeys the anchor.

criteria.yes: The item text says PORT-010 produces no finding for a `#[cfg(unix)] mod ...;` declaration or shape S6, in any wording such as stop reporting, no longer reports, exempt, skip, yields no finding, treat as unix-only by design, or a test asserting zero findings on the declaration line.

addressed.instructions: Does `item.text` state that PORT-010 will not report the declaration line of a `#[cfg(unix)] mod x;` module (#786 shape S6) because that module is never compiled on Windows? The item must name the module-declaration case specifically and state the no-report outcome. A general promise to fix #786 or PORT-010 false positives, a refactor that states no outcome, a deferral, or exempting only the items inside the module does not count. Judge presence of this outcome only, not conflict.

criteria.no: The item text says nothing that leaves the declaration reported: it stops reporting it, does not mention it, defers it, or concerns other work.
criteria.unclear: The item text touches the declaration handling in a way that might leave it reported, but it cannot be told.
criteria.yes: The item text states that PORT-010 will continue to report the `#[cfg(unix)] mod ...;` declaration, or that consumers must suppress that declaration's finding.

contradicted.instructions: Does `item.text` plan an outcome in which PORT-010 still reports the declaration line of a `#[cfg(unix)] mod x;` module (#786 shape S6)? Conflict includes keeping or restoring that report, leaving the declaration reported while exempting only the module's inner items, or requiring consumers to silence the declaration with a per-site allow, a configuration exclusion, or a disabled rule. Silence about the declaration, deferring S6 to later work, work on other shapes, and unrelated work are not conflict. Judge conflict only.

results.statement: sc-lint's PORT-010 (sc-lint's rule that reports a production #[cfg(unix)] item lacking a #[cfg(windows)] companion or portable fallback) changes must not blanket-suppress real parity gaps: a production #[cfg(unix)] item with no #[cfg(windows)] companion and no portable fallback must still be reported.
results.quote:
REQ-PRODUCT-004AA/PORT-010 (docs/requirements.md): "`PORT-010` - production structural `#[cfg(unix)]` companion-parity checks"

ADR-010 decision 6 (Accepted): "Explicit `#[cfg(unix)]` production boundaries are treated as structural parity questions for the shared portability family. Leaf rules may suppress inside those items, with the companion-or-fallback decision owned by the structural parity rule family instead of parallel per-rule allowlists."

Issue #786 (atm-core verdict table, 2026-10-30): "#720 covers only the crate-root main.rs shape; this issue tracks the complete remaining inventory and asks for per-case classification, not blanket suppression of real parity gaps."
results.context: Phase M v3: requirement/ADR-based derivation under ADR-022 direction, 2026-10-30; candidate P9

results.statement: PORT-010, a rule sc-lint's portability analyzer reports from source, must be allowable at a single site: an item carrying #[sc_lint(allow(PORT-010), reason = "...")] is not reported by PORT-010.
results.quote: ADR-022 (Rand 2026-10-30: "This is a positive step.  This should guide both anchors and decisions about how atm-core fixes are handled.  Proceed"), decision 4: "Every rule an analyzer reports from source can be allowed at a single site with `#[sc_lint(allow(<RULE>), reason = \"...\")]`. A site allowance is the approved exception path for a deliberate, non-parity case such as #786 S8."
results.stated_by: ADR-022 decision 4 + #786 S8 + Rand S8 ruling
results.context: Phase M v3: requirement/ADR-based derivation under ADR-022 direction, 2026-10-30; candidate P10c

criteria.yes: The item adds, changes, removes or reworks PORT-010's handling of a per-site #[sc_lint(allow(...))] allowance, including parsing allow(PORT-010) or replacing per-item PORT-010 allowances with another mechanism.

addressed.instructions: Does `item.text` commit to this outcome, either as new work or by keeping it working: an item that carries `#[sc_lint(allow(PORT-010), reason = "...")]` is not reported by PORT-010? Accept words such as honour, skip, suppress, exempt, records no finding, or not reported for the annotated item, function or declaration. Silence about site allowances, planning only to investigate them, requiring the `reason`, or limiting the allowance to the annotated item or to the PORT-010 rule is not a conflict. Judge conflict only.

results.statement: A [[tool.sc-lint.lint]] step in sc-lint.toml must accept an env table and a cwd key, applied to that step's child process, with the same meaning they have on a test command selector.
results.quote:
ADR-016 (Accepted), How To Extend: "Use declarative `sc-lint.toml` lint profiles, test layers, per-analyzer tables, step argv/exclusions, platform conditionals and per-step/per-layer `env`."

ADR-022 (Rand 2026-10-30: "This is a positive step.  This should guide both anchors and decisions about how atm-core fixes are handled.  Proceed"), decision 3.2: "Parallel constructs accept parallel keys. A lint step and a test command selector accept the same execution keys: `command`, `env`, `cwd`, platform restriction and `after_all`."
results.stated_by: ADR-016 How To Extend + ADR-022 decision 3.2 + #198
results.context: Phase M v3: requirement/ADR-based derivation under ADR-022 direction, 2026-10-30; candidate P11

relevant.instructions: Does `item.text` work on sc-lint's `[[tool.sc-lint.lint]]` lint steps? Signals: the item names lint steps or `[[tool.sc-lint.lint]]`, adds or rejects a lint-step key, or changes how the lint runner spawns a step's command. Work on a lint rule such as PORT-010 or SCB-MANIFEST-004 is not work on lint steps. Answer about subject matter only; do not judge whether the item follows `anchor.statement`.

criteria.no: The item does not plan that behaviour: it is silent about it, names only the issue or lint-step configuration in general, adds a different key, supports only one of `env` and `cwd`, or keeps lint steps rejecting them.

criteria.yes: The item says lint steps accept `env` and `cwd` (environment variables and working directory, in any wording) and that they apply to the step's command or child process, or that lint steps share the test command selector's handling of these keys.

addressed.instructions: `anchor.statement` requires one specific behaviour: a `[[tool.sc-lint.lint]]` step accepts both an `env` table and a `cwd` key, and sc-lint applies them to that step's child process with the same meaning they have on a test command selector. Does `item.text` plan for, or state as an outcome, that behaviour, with both `env` and `cwd`? Judge presence of this behaviour only; do not judge conflict.

criteria.no: Nothing in the item conflicts: it follows the requirement, is silent about it, adds or rejects other keys, or concerns other work.
criteria.unclear: The item describes lint-step keys in a way that might or might not leave `env` or `cwd` unsupported.
criteria.yes: The item states that lint steps reject or do not support `env` or `cwd`, or gives them a meaning other than setting the step's child environment and working directory.

contradicted.instructions: `anchor.statement` requires `[[tool.sc-lint.lint]]` steps to accept an `env` table and a `cwd` key, applied to the step's child process with the same meaning as on test command selectors. Does `item.text` plan or state something that cannot be reconciled with that requirement, for example lint steps still rejecting `env` or `cwd`, lint steps limited to keys that exclude them, or env/cwd applied somewhere other than the step's child process? Silence is not conflict. Adding a different key is not conflict. Continuing to reject other unknown keys is not conflict. Judge conflict only.
